subject: Re: Post-call: MedCore Health 14 private VPC data flow & PII reqs

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jacob Reed <jacob.reed@medcorehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 17:15:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap: MedCore Health 14 private VPC data flow & PII reqs

Hi Jacob / Anita,

Thanks again for taking time today — great to understand the product/team priorities. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we can keep momentum: 

1) Scope & desired outcome
- You want a Private (VPC) deployment of Redwood for MedCore's clinical note ingestion and triage pipeline. Primary goals: zero PHI egress, auditable access logs, and 7-year retention controls per your policy.

2) Key technical questions we committed to follow up on (see attached network diagram stub):
- A: Network boundaries — do you prefer customer-managed subnets with our nodes peered, or a managed-hosted VPC where we operate inside your account?
- B: Egress controls — confirm that all outbound traffic must be blocked except to Redwood-managed update endpoints (if allowed) and your approved telemetry sinks.
- C: On-prem / air-gapped constraints — you mentioned a possible air-gapped processing stage for PHI. Need to confirm whether model invocation will occur on-prem or if you can accept encrypted-in-transit requests to a private VPC in your cloud.

3) Compliance artifacts we attached for initial review:
- Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf (summary + auditor contact)
- Redwood_Private_VPC_MA_v1.pdf (draft mutual action plan)
- MedCore_network_diagram_v1.pdf (you shared during the call; adding to thread)

4) Proposed next steps / owners
- Jacob / Anita: confirm preferred hosting pattern (customer VPC peering vs Redwood-hosted inside your account) and whether the ingestion service will always be behind your internal NAT/proxy (by 2026-04-02).
- Dev (cc'd): will map out the high-level egress rules we need and outline options for offline / on-prem model invocation.
- Laura (cc'd): will prepare a tech-runbook draft + estimate for deployment effort.
- Neha (cc'd): will review data processing terms and identify any contract redlines you should anticipate.

If you'd like, we can set a 30-minute follow-up with Dev and Laura next week to walk the network diagram and runtime controls. 

Thanks — looking forward to your confirmation on the hosting preference.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0172

Attachments: MedCore_network_diagram_v1.pdf, Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf, Redwood_Private_VPC_MA_v1.pdf

From: Jacob Reed <jacob.reed@medcorehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Anita Singh <anita.singh@medcorehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: MedCore Health 14 private VPC data flow & PII reqs

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Hosting pattern: our security team prefers the "customer-managed VPC" model (we want to control routing & firewall rules inside our account). Can Redwood operate with nodes deployed in our project/account with customer-side peering?

- Egress: all outbound egress must be blocked by default. The only exceptions we'd consider are: 1) to a Redwood signer for verified model updates (explicit IPs), and 2) to our internal telemetry collector (CloudWatch/Datadog endpoint) — both must be whitelisted on our side.

- On-prem invocation: for certain high-risk datasets, we will use an on-prem processing step. Ideally, Redwood would provide an offline (batch) inference option that runs inside our air-gapped environment (or allow you to ship a hardened appliance). Is that supported?

- Retention & logging: we need per-tenant access logs with immutable timestamps and the ability to set retention to 7 years for audit logs. Also need confirmation that user content (PHI) will not be copied into any Redwood-hosted analytics or model training stores.

Can Dev / Laura / Neha respond on feasibility and any constraints? If it helps, we can get our security architect on the follow-up call next Wednesday.

Jacob
Jacob Reed
Head of Platform Security | MedCore Health
jacob.reed@medcorehealth.com

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jacob Reed <jacob.reed@medcorehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 19:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: MedCore Health 14 private VPC data flow & PII reqs

Hi Jacob — good questions. Short answers up front, followed by constraints and proposed approaches.

Short answers: 
- Customer-managed VPC: supported. We can deploy Redwood private workers into your AWS account using a controller/operator that you run (IAM role + CloudFormation/Terraform) or via a cross-account deployment pattern where we request minimal VPC resources and you keep control of subnet/route tables.
- Egress controls: we can support deny-by-default egress with an allowlist for specific update endpoints and telemetry. All outbound egress from the inference worker can be proxied through your NAT/Gateway so you control whitelisting.
- On-prem / air-gapped: we offer two options: 1) an on-prem dockerized runtime for batch inference (air-gapped) — supports scheduled batch jobs only (no streaming real-time) OR 2) a hardened appliance bundle (requires procurement lead time). We do not currently support full real-time model training inside an air-gapped env.
- Retention & logging: we can ship immutable, signed access logs and configure log retention policies up to 10 years. By default we do not use customer content for model training; we can include a contract clause and technical controls (no-copy ingestion pipeline + SSE-KMS with your key).

Constraints / details: 
- Management plane: if you want Redwood to push security patches automatically we need a restricted set of outbound endpoints for updates (we can also provide an allowlist and manual update workflow).
- Live streaming: real-time low-latency streaming inside a pure air-gapped network is not supported unless you accept a customer-deployed worker in your environment that we provide as a vetted container image.
- Appliance: appliance option requires hardware compatibility and on-site support plan (we can share SOW/estimate).

Next actions I propose: 
1) Laura to send a one-page deployment pattern matrix (customer-VPC peering vs operator in account vs Redwood-hosted) with effort estimates.
2) Neha to circulate the specific contract language and a short data processing addendum for the "no use for training" clause.
3) Let's schedule a technical follow-up with your security architect — I'm available Wed 2026-04-01 17:00-19:00 UTC.

I'll attach a short tech note and the minimal firewall rules we need.

Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: Redwood_deployment_options_technote.pdf

Also please confirm the "no-copy for training" technical control and whether you can provide a signed DPA addendum prior to PoC kickoff.

Thanks,
Anita
